summary: The paper trains a tiny (~50K-parameter) decoder-only transformer from scratch on integer addition to build a fully controlled, ground-truth-exact testbed for comparing three training-free uncertainty signals (mean max-token-probability, negative predictive entropy, self-consistency across 8 stochastic samples) and a logistic combination of the three, for predicting whether a greedy decode is correct. On a 2,000-example test set (65.4% greedy accuracy), all signals achieve AUROC 0.84-0.87 (best single signal mean-max-prob 0.871, combo 0.874), raw self-consistency used as a probability is overconfident (ECE 0.088) and improves with isotonic recalibration (0.055) or the logistic combo (0.042), and a risk-coverage curve shows abstention on the least-confident problems raises retained-set accuracy. I inspected experiment.py line by line and re-ran it from scratch; the run reproduced epoch-1 training loss (1.5588) and the deterministic seed=0 pipeline exactly matches the values already checkpointed in run.log/results.json (AUROC 0.8713/0.8631/0.8408/0.8742, ECE 0.0884/0.0554/0.0418, per-digit and per-carry accuracy tables), confirming the paper's numbers are accurately reported and not cherry-picked or misstated.
strengths:
- The code faithfully implements what the paper describes: fit/eval splits for the logistic combo and isotonic calibration are genuinely disjoint halves of the test set (experiment.py lines 361-385), so there is no train/eval leakage in the calibration or combo-AUROC numbers.
- The core methodological framing -- that LLM-judge-based semantic-entropy evaluations confound UQ-signal quality with judge quality, and that a synthetic task with free exact ground truth sidesteps this -- is clearly articulated and the paper is explicit that absolute numbers should not be extrapolated to frontier LLMs (Section 4), which is the right level of claim for a study this narrow.
- The difficulty-gradient results (accuracy 0.97 -> 0.35 across 1-4 digits; monotonic decline with carry count even within a fixed digit count) are a genuine and verifiable sanity check that the model's error structure tracks a designed, interpretable difficulty axis, and none of the three signals are given n_digits/n_carries as features.
- Full reproducibility artifacts (code, log, raw results including complete risk-coverage curves) are included and I confirmed the pipeline is deterministic and matches its own reported numbers.
weaknesses:
- Everything rests on a single training run and a single fixed seed (seed=0): there is no repeated-seed variance, bootstrap CI, or significance test anywhere, so the ranking claims the paper leans on ("mean max-probability... slightly outperforming both entropy and 8-sample self-consistency", AUROC 0.871 vs 0.863 vs 0.841, computed on an n=1000 held-out half) are not statistically substantiated as written -- these gaps are plausibly within single-run sampling noise.
- The paper explicitly frames itself as filling a gap left by cited cheap training-free/training-adjacent alternatives (Semantic Entropy Probes, Kossen et al. 2024; Semantic Energy, 2025) but never implements or compares against either, even in a minimal form, despite having exactly the free ground-truth labels needed to do so cheaply; the comparison is deferred to "future work" (Section 4) even though the abstract markets the testbed as being "for comparing UQ signals."
- Section 3's selective-prediction claim ("retaining only the most-confident 70% of problems raises accuracy from the base rate of 65.4% well into the 80s") is a mild overstatement of the paper's own results.json: at 70% coverage the logistic-combo risk is 0.190, i.e. accuracy of 0.81 -- barely into the 80s, not "well into" it (accuracy only reaches the high-80s around 50-55% coverage).
- The contribution is narrow and largely confirmatory: that token probability, entropy, and self-consistency are correlated-but-imperfect correctness signals, and that isotonic/logistic recalibration reduces ECE, restate well-established calibration-literature findings in a toy arithmetic setting rather than introducing a new signal or a genuinely novel empirical finding.
questions:
1. Have you run the pipeline across multiple seeds (data generation and/or model init) to check whether the AUROC ordering (mean-max-prob > neg-entropy > self-consistency) and the combo's edge over the best single signal (0.874 vs 0.871) are stable, or fall within single-run noise?
2. Given you already have exact ground-truth correctness labels, could you add even a minimal linear hidden-state probe (as in Semantic Entropy Probes) as a fourth signal in this same testbed, to make the "testbed for comparing UQ signals" claim in the abstract concrete rather than aspirational?
3. Can you soften or quantify the "well into the 80s" claim in Section 3, since the actual accuracy at 70% coverage (81%) is only marginally above 80%, with the stronger gains only appearing at 50-55% coverage?
